newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT--CBOT Aug soybeans firm on tight supplies.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT--CBOT Aug soybeans firm on tight supplies.

text.p: Concerns of tight old crop soybean supplies drove Chicago Board of Trade August soybean futures sharply higher this week and more volatility was expected before the contract expires on Wednesday, Aug 20, oilseed analysts said.

"The shorts are on the run and it's going to be extremely volatile," said one oilseed analyst who, like others, declined to be named. "We still have quite a bit of open interest left ahead of expiry."
The August contract peaked at $7.92 per bushel early Friday, up more than 50 cents from last Friday's close.

Preliminary CBOT data showed open interest in the August fell by 7.2 million bushels as of Thursday's day session close but remained at a hefty 21.8 million bushels, a level analysts and traders said was still too high for comfort.
CBOT data indicates there will not be a large amount of soybeans registered and delivered against the August contract.
According to CBOT records, as of Thursday there was a total of 65,000 bushels of soybeans registered for delivery at elevators in Toledo, St. Louis and Chicago.

As of last Friday, only 2,703,000 bushels of soybeans were in warehouses in those locations and classified as deliverable grades against the CBOT contract. Daily CBOT data of receipts and shipments has shown net Chicago shipments of soybeans this week.
"We ought to lose five to seven million (bushels in open interest) a day and go into the last trading day with something under 10 million," a veteran CBOT floor trader said.
Open interest in August soybeans fell 23.5 million bushels in the five trading days ending Thursday, an average 4.7 million bushels a day.

Meanwhile, there were indications demand for dwindling old crop supplies remained strong. The U.S. Agriculture Department said Tuesday old crop soybean stocks would fall to 125 million bushels by the end of August, the lowest level in 20 years.
The National Oilseed Processors Association on Friday said there were 24.341 million bushels of soybeans crushed in the week of August 13, above trade expectations.

NOPA also said there were 104.897 million bushels of soybeans crushed during the month of July. Trade sources said they had expected that figure to come in between 102.3 million and 103.5 million bushels.

"The weekly and monthly crush numbers are still showing demand out there and there is talk of boats waiting to load at the Gulf," a Chicago-based oilseeds analyst said. "The farmers haven't been real aggressive sellers, so the people who need it are going to have to pay for it."
Cash basis levels continued to firm both at country elevator locations and at export points. Grain dealers said bids were up early Friday in parts of Iowa and Illinois.
Export sources said CIF barge bids at the U.S. Gulf were also up sharply for prompt shipment.

"The river levels have been rather firm with the crushers competing with the elevator locations," an analyst said. "The processors have backed off a bit today but I don't see (spot prices) really falling apart until everyone is satisfied that we have the supplies to meet immediate demands."
